chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Aban, from the one who mentioned it, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) who said:
It was said to him: A certain man in Medina bought a slave who had children, and he freed them, so he said: 'I dislike that I should attract their Wilayah (manumission bond).'.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The reason for the dislike in attracting the Wilayah is that the Wilayah is not established except when the manumission is for the sake of God Almighty. As for when the manumission is obligatory or is a Sā'ibah, then the Wilayah is not established by it.

And if the matter is thus, it is disliked that a man free a slave in order to attract the Wilayah of his children to himself, without intending thereby the face of God Almighty. Rather, it is proper that he intend by the manumission the seeking of God's pleasure purely, and that the Wilayah be a follower [subsidiary] to it.

key_terms.اَلْوَلاَء: Manumission bond; the legal relationship between a master and the freed slave.
key_terms.اِبْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاةِ اَللَّهِ: Seeking the pleasure of God; the ideal intention for acts of worship and charity.
key_terms.سَائِبَة: A type of manumission where the slave is freed unconditionally, often with the intention of the master being supported by the freed slave.
key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اَللَّهِ: For the sake of God; done purely for divine pleasure without worldly motive.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for establishing the manumission bond (Wilayah) when freeing a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam Ali al-Hadi (AS) via the chain of An-Nadr and Aban, highlighting the juristic distinction between manumission performed for God's sake versus that done to secure a social bond (wilayah) for one's offspring. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan elaborates that while the bond is established in all cases, it is disliked (makruh) to free a slave with the primary intent of acquiring the children's loyalty rather than seeking divine pleasure, as the bond should be a consequence of sincerity, not the motive.
